text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — final tiebreaker for Optimize toolkit prioritization. We have two urgent customer asks (AcmeHealth: strict p99 SLA; Sequoia: cost-sensitivity) and a backlog: batching improvements, prefix/KV caching guidance, quantization recommendations, and eval-triggered alerts. Meeting in 30 to pick an order.

Jorge: Short take — batching reduces per-token express latency for high-concurrency; caching gives biggest unit-cost gains for repetitive prompts; quant recs are higher-risk (quality regression). If a customer will churn without SLA met, push batching first.

Lin: Ops data FYI — last 3 weeks we saw p99 spikes at 22:00 UTC when concurrency hits 35-50 for several tenants. Quick numbers:
```
baseline p99: 420ms
with naive batching (batch-size 8): p99 -> 310ms
with batching+adaptive-shards: p99 -> 260ms (but ~5% request queueing increase at tail)
```
So batching helps but we need guardrails to avoid queuing regressions.

Sam: From eval harness: model-x quant -> 2-bit (aggressive) regressed on negation and numeric accuracy. 4-bit LLMQ maintains parity on test suite. Suggest we only recommend 4-bit for general guidance and run a small A/B for 2-bit on permissive customers.

Ashley: @Maya Customer context: AcmeHealth is explicit—pilot must keep p99 < 250ms or they won't proceed to Dedicated. Sequoia gave a usage profile: 60% repeated prompts (cacheable) and cares about 40% cost reduction target.

Maya: Proposed tiebreaker rubric to apply now:
1) Customer SLA risk (churn / pilot stop) — binary urgent flag
2) Measured unit-cost delta (estimated tokens saved / month)
3) Rollout complexity (runtime changes vs console guidance)
4) Quality/regression risk (eval deltas)
Apply in that order; if #1 triggers for any paying pilot, escalate to top priority.

Ryan: Design note — expose a compact "cost vs latency" preview in Console (slider shows estimated p99 and $/1M tokens) so customers can self-select tradeoffs; that reduces support load for the first wave.

Jorge: Rough engineering estimates (T-shirt -> sprint count):
- Batching infra + adaptive shard rollout + canary: 3 sprints (core runtime + tests + Ops runbook)
- Prefix/KV caching recommendations (advisor + lightweight runtime caching): 2 sprints (mostly product + small runtime hooks)
- Quantization recommendations + eval matrix + opt-in A/B infra: 4 sprints (model onboarding + eval+docs)
- Eval-triggered alerts (integration with Eval Sentry + Ops flows): 2 sprints (backend + console)

Maya: Suggested launch waves (proposal):
Wave 1 (ship in 6-8 weeks): batching quick wins (bounded batching, adaptive shards), caching guidance + console cost-preview, run AcmeHealth private pilot with canary.
Wave 2 (follow-up 2-3 sprints): formalize quantization recommendations (4-bit baseline), eval-triggered alerts, and A/B infra for aggressive quant pilots.

Ashley: That sequence aligns w/ customer asks. If AcmeHealth tolerates a short SLA exemption for pilot setup window, we can parallelize caching work to get cost wins faster.

Maya: Draft launch acceptance (we'll formalize in PR):
- Acceptance: p99 for pilot tenants meets agreed SLA (<250ms for AcmeHealth) under 95th percentile traffic patterns
- Unit-cost estimate validated against simulated load and within +/-15% of pre-launch model
- No eval regressions >3% on critical test suites for released quant recs
- Ops runbook and automatic fallback (route to unquantized model) present

Jorge: I'll sketch an engineering cut that allows batching toggle per-tenant and a low-risk fallback to preserve availability.

deploy-bot: Meeting scheduled — roadmap tiebreaker check-in in :30 (link: https://meet.redwood.internal/optimize-tiebreaker)

Maya: Decision for today's triage: prioritize Wave 1 as defined, treat quantization recs as Wave 2, and send the acceptance criteria to stakeholders. I'll open the PR with scope slices and the rollout plan now. :thumbsup:
